articles.title: Has China made a better electric Ferrari than Ferrari?
articles.summary: Ferrari's controversial all-electric Luce, designed in collaboration with Apple alumni, has drawn scrutiny as the marque attempts to transition into the electric era. The vehicle represents Ferrari's most significant departure from tradition, featuring Apple-influenced design language that has polarized enthusiasts and investors alike.

articles.title: OpenAI's CFO says she can't say if Jony Ive's device is an earpiece
articles.summary: OpenAI CFO Sarah Friar declined to confirm whether the highly anticipated AI device being developed with Jony Ive takes the form of an earpiece. The statement represents one of the few public acknowledgments from OpenAI regarding the specifics of their collaboration with the former Apple design chief.

articles.title: Flush With Cash From OpenAI, Opal Is Making an AI-Powered Audio Gadget
articles.summary: Opal Electronics, previously known for premium webcams, has secured substantial investment from OpenAI and Samsung to develop an AI-powered audio device. The pivot marks the company's expansion into consumer electronics, leveraging OpenAI's backing to enter the emerging AI hardware market.

articles.title: Jony Ive Discusses Ferrari Luce Design [VIDEO]
articles.summary: Jony Ive has provided rare public commentary on his design work for Ferrari's Luce, the 1,035-horsepower all-electric supercar that deliberately eschews touchscreens in favor of tactile interfaces. The collaboration represents Ive's most high-profile automotive project since departing Apple, applying his minimalist philosophy to Ferrari's electric transformation.

articles.title: Slate Money - Least Cool Ferrari Ever
articles.summary: Ferrari's new electric vehicle, the Luce, designed by Jony Ive, has become an internet meme following its poor reception at the $640,000 price point. The design backlash was so severe it triggered a significant drop in Ferrari's stock price, raising questions about the collaboration between the former Apple design chief and the Italian luxury automaker.

articles.title: Ferrari Announce Their First EV
articles.summary: Ferrari has unveiled the Luce, its first fully electric vehicle, featuring design work by former Apple design chief Jony Ive through his LoveFrom studio. The five-seat, four-door vehicle is powered by four electric motors producing 1,035 horsepower, marking Ferrari's entry into the EV market with a radical departure from traditional sports car design.

articles.title: Jony Ive-Designed Ferrari Luce Tests CEO Benedetto Vigna’s EV Bet
articles.summary: Ferrari's Luce EV has drawn harsh criticism from designers, fans, and former chairman Luca di Montezemolo, exposing the risks of CEO Benedetto Vigna's strategy to reinvent Ferrari's visual language. Despite the bruising debut of Jony Ive's design, the vehicle may still attract ultra-wealthy buyers willing to pay premium prices for exclusivity.

articles.title: Everything We Know About OpenAI's Planned iPhone Rival
articles.summary: OpenAI is developing a smartphone designed to compete directly with the iPhone, representing a significant shift from the company's previous hardware strategy. Analyst Ming-Chi Kuo has published findings on the project, which marks OpenAI's ambitious move into consumer hardware beyond AI software applications.

articles.title: How Ferrari bungled the design of its first EV
articles.summary: Ferrari's Luce EV, designed by Jony Ive, has fundamentally challenged the brand's nearly 80-year cultural position as an aspirational luxury icon. The design backlash threatens Ferrari's unique ability to maintain desirability even among those who resent its exclusivity, suggesting a potential miscalculation in the brand's evolution toward electrification.

articles.title: Jony Ive’s funky Ferrari
articles.summary: Ferrari's first electric vehicle, the Luce, represents one of the year's most surprising automotive designs with its decidedly un-Ferrari aesthetic shaped by Jony Ive. Despite most consumers never experiencing the vehicle firsthand, its radical departure from traditional Ferrari design language has generated significant industry discussion about the future of luxury automotive design.

articles.title: Ferrari's First EV Gets Pope Leo's Blessing, but Everyone Else Hates It
articles.summary: Ferrari's first electric vehicle, the Luce, has received a polarizing public reception despite earning an unusual papal blessing. The four-door sedan underwent a design transformation with assistance from Jony Ive's LoveFrom studio.

articles.title: All the news about Ferrari’s polarizing Luce EV
articles.summary: Ferrari's Luce EV, designed with input from Jony Ive's LoveFrom, has provoked fierce criticism from traditionalist Ferrari enthusiasts who reject its departure from the marque's aesthetic heritage. The electric four-door sedan represents a stark divergence from Ferrari's sporting DNA, with critics arguing that Ive's minimalist Apple design philosophy proves incompatible with automotive passion.

archive.title: I Like Ferrari's Luce EV. But This Is Why It's Heartbreaking
archive.summary: The Ferrari Luce EV, designed by Jony Ive and former Apple colleagues, offers a tantalizing glimpse into what might have emerged from Apple's abandoned $10 billion automotive venture. While the author appreciates the design execution, the project underscores the lost potential of Apple's ultimately scrapped car program.

archive.title: Ferrari's first EV is ruthlessly mocked, described as 'straight to the junkyard trash' and even condemned by former boss - as share price slumps
archive.summary: Ferrari's £474,320 Luce EV has triggered savage criticism from enthusiasts and industry veterans, with detractors dismissing the LoveFrom-designed vehicle as worthless. The backlash has been so severe that Ferrari's share price has declined following the unveiling of its first five-seater electric vehicle.

archive.title: Memes race to poke fun at Jony Ive’s new Ferrari Luce design
archive.summary: Jony Ive's Ferrari Luce design has already spawned a wave of internet memes and fierce debate within days of its unveiling. The electric vehicle represents the closest realization of what an Apple car might have resembled, given Ive's central role in the project.

archive.title: Ferrari Reveals Luce, Its First Fully Electric Vehicle, Co-Designed by Jony Ive
archive.summary: Ferrari unveiled the Luce, its first fully electric vehicle co-designed by Jony Ive's LoveFrom studio, marking a significant departure from traditional Ferrari aesthetics. The launch comes as other luxury automakers retreat from EV plans, with public reception proving sharply polarized. The collaboration represents Ferrari's belated entry into the electric vehicle market with the backing of Apple's former chief design officer.

archive.title: The Ferrari Luce will have Samsung OLED displays with holes and stacked design
archive.summary: The Ferrari Luce features multiple Samsung-manufactured OLED displays with advanced hole-punch and stacked designs throughout its interior. Sir Jony Ive's LoveFrom studio designed both the exterior and interior of the vehicle, integrating sophisticated display technology as a central element of the user experience.

archive.title: Jony Ive’s Ferrari looks nothing like a Ferrari
archive.summary: Jony Ive's design for Ferrari's first electric vehicle, the Luce, represents a radical aesthetic departure from the brand's traditional design language. The collaboration highlights Ferrari's unusually late entry into the EV market, coming at a time when most automakers have scaled back their electric ambitions.

archive.title: Sir Jony Ive on Designing the Incredible UI of Ferrari's New EV
archive.summary: Ferrari entrusted the design of their inaugural EV, the Luce, to LoveFrom, the design collective led by Sir Jony Ive and Marc Newson. The decision to engage an external design firm for such a pivotal vehicle represents an unprecedented move for Ferrari's traditionally insular design process.

archive.title: iPhone designer Jony Ive's first full car is the electric Ferrari Luce
archive.summary: Ferrari unveiled the Luce, its first fully electric vehicle co-designed by Jony Ive and Marc Newson at LoveFrom, marking the luxury carmaker's dramatic entry into the EV market. The five-seat electric supercar delivers 1,035 horsepower and accelerates from 0-60 mph in 2.5 seconds, representing a complete departure from Ferrari's traditional design language. Starting at €550,000, the Luce begins deliveries in the fourth quarter of 2026.

archive.title: Ferrari Reveals $640,000 EV Co-Designed by Jony Ive
archive.summary: Apple's former design chief Jony Ive and his LoveFrom studio collaborated with Ferrari to create a singular design language that unites the exterior and interior of the $640,000 Luce electric vehicle. The partnership represents Ive's most significant automotive project since leaving Apple, demonstrating his design philosophy applied to luxury electric mobility. Ferrari positioned the collaboration as central to reimagining what an electric Ferrari could represent in the luxury automotive space.

archive.title: ferrari unveils luce, its first electric car designed by jony ive and marc newson
archive.summary: LoveFrom's Jony Ive and Marc Newson designed Ferrari's inaugural electric vehicle with distinctive rear-hinged doors and a revolutionary five-seat layout that breaks from traditional Ferrari conventions. The Luce features LoveFrom-designed controls integrated throughout the cabin, showcasing the design studio's automotive capabilities beyond their previous consumer electronics work. The collaboration marks the first complete vehicle designed by Ive's studio since its founding after his departure from Apple.

archive.title: OpenAI's new AI-focused smartphone is taking aim at Apple's iPhone
archive.summary: OpenAI is developing an AI-first smartphone designed to challenge Apple's iPhone, featuring collaboration with Jony Ive and custom silicon from Qualcomm and MediaTek. The device represents OpenAI's ambitious push into hardware, moving beyond software to create integrated AI-native experiences. This marks a significant escalation in the competition between AI companies and traditional smartphone manufacturers.

archive.title: Is OpenAI launching a mobile phone? Here’s the lowdown
archive.summary: OpenAI has reportedly accelerated development of its AI agent smartphone, targeting mass production for early 2027. The device aims to transcend current assistant-driven phones by enabling autonomous agents that can independently handle complex tasks without user intervention. This represents a fundamental shift from reactive AI helpers to proactive digital agents embedded in mobile hardware.

archive.title: OpenAI is reportedly launching a phone for ChatGPT
archive.summary: OpenAI's first hardware product may be a smartphone rather than the mysterious device being developed with Jony Ive, according to supply chain analyst Ming-Chi Kuo. The company is reportedly fast-tracking the phone's development with plans to begin mass production in the coming years. This suggests OpenAI is pursuing multiple hardware initiatives simultaneously, with the smartphone potentially launching ahead of Ive's undisclosed project.

archive.title: OpenAI’s new phone being fast-tracked to launch next year, per report
archive.summary: OpenAI is accelerating development of its smartphone to compete directly with the iPhone, according to updated reports from analyst Ming-Chi Kuo. The company is moving faster than initially anticipated to launch its first phone, suggesting increased urgency in OpenAI's hardware ambitions. This timeline acceleration indicates growing confidence in the company's ability to challenge established mobile platforms with AI-native hardware.

archive.title: OpenAI Said to Be Making Phone With AI Agents to Replace Apps
archive.summary: OpenAI is reportedly developing a smartphone that would replace traditional apps with AI agents, marking the company's entry into hardware manufacturing. The device represents a fundamental shift from app-based mobile experiences to AI-driven interactions, according to industry reports.

archive.title: This 20th Anniversary iPhone rumor is speculative but persuasive
archive.summary: Speculation around Apple's 20th anniversary iPhone centers on former design chief Jony Ive's long-term vision of the device as a single slab of glass. The rumor reflects Ive's aesthetic philosophy of prioritizing sleek design over functional complexity, though his approach was sometimes criticized as excessive.

archive.title: Inside OpenAI’s $6 Billion Plan to Build the Ultimate AI Phone
archive.summary: OpenAI's reported $6 billion smartphone initiative aims to integrate artificial intelligence directly into hardware rather than relying on conventional app ecosystems. The project represents a significant departure from traditional smartphone design philosophy, focusing on AI-first user experiences.

archive.title: OpenAI is building a phone that would make apps obsolete. The supply chain says it might actually ship.
archive.summary: OpenAI is developing a smartphone centered on AI agents rather than traditional apps, with Qualcomm and MediaTek jointly designing a custom processor and Luxshare Precision handling manufacturing, according to supply chain analyst Ming-Chi Kuo. The device represents a fundamental reimagining of mobile interaction, replacing the app-based paradigm with AI-driven task completion. This marks a significant pivot for OpenAI, which had previously denied plans to enter the smartphone market.

archive.title: Could This New AI Smartphone Compete With Apple? Qualcomm Shares Rise
archive.summary: OpenAI's smartphone development appears linked to Sam Altman's vision for AI "companions," a project that gained momentum after the company recruited Apple's former design chief Jony Ive last year. The news sent Qualcomm shares higher on speculation about the chip partnership. The timing suggests Ive's involvement may be instrumental in shaping OpenAI's hardware ambitions beyond the previously rumored standalone AI device.

archive.title: OpenAI Reportedly Working on an AI Smartphone to Rival iPhone
archive.summary: Supply chain analyst Ming-Chi Kuo reports that OpenAI has reversed course and is now actively developing a smartphone to compete with the iPhone, contradicting earlier denials from the company. The project represents a significant strategic shift as OpenAI moves beyond software into hardware competition with Apple. Kuo's supply chain intelligence suggests concrete manufacturing partnerships are already in place, lending credibility to the smartphone's potential reality.

archive.title: BMW’s Design Boss Says Ferrari Just Proved Him Right About Physical Buttons
archive.summary: BMW's design chief Adrian van Hooydonk has cited Ferrari's return to physical buttons as validation of his position against touchscreen interfaces, invoking Jony Ive's design philosophy in the ongoing automotive interface debate. The statement represents a broader industry shift away from screen-dominated cockpits toward tactile controls, with luxury automakers leading the retreat from digital-first design paradigms.

archive.title: Apple awards rare $200K–$400K bonuses to iPhone designers to stem exodus to OpenAI
archive.summary: Apple has distributed exceptional retention bonuses ranging from $200,000 to $400,000 to its iPhone hardware design team as designers increasingly defect to OpenAI and other AI startups. The unprecedented compensation reflects the company's growing concern over talent hemorrhaging to competitors developing AI-native hardware products.

archive.title: Where is defining gadget of AI age? Jony Ive, former design chief of Apple, is working on his toughest assignment yet, give AI a physique
archive.summary: Jony Ive faces his most challenging design brief since the iPhone: creating a physical form factor for artificial intelligence in collaboration with OpenAI. The project represents an attempt to define the AI era's signature device, as early AI hardware efforts have largely failed to capture consumer imagination or achieve commercial success.

archive.title: iyO amends lawsuit against OpenAI’s io, now alleges trade secret theft
archive.summary: iyO has amended its lawsuit against OpenAI's hardware division io, now alleging that former Apple designer Tang Tan—who co-founded io—was given access to confidential designs that constitute trade secret theft. The expanded legal complaint broadens the initial scope of iyO's case against OpenAI's hardware ambitions.

archive.title: Apple Gives iPhone Designers Bonuses Up to $400K to Counter OpenAI Poaching
archive.summary: Apple distributed bonuses worth up to $400,000 in restricted stock units to its iPhone Product Design team to prevent talent defection to competitors, particularly OpenAI. The retention effort, totaling between $200-400 million, comes as OpenAI aggressively recruits Apple's hardware designers for its consumer device projects.

archive.title: "Anything good is kind of costly" says Marc Newson
archive.summary: Marc Newson, Jony Ive's longtime collaborator and LoveFrom co-founder, reflects on four decades of design practice in a new interview, discussing affordability in luxury design and his current projects including Ferrari's first electric vehicle. Newson, whose work became the most expensive piece ever sold at auction by a living designer, maintains that "anything good is kind of costly."

archive.title: Meet the former Apple designer building a new AI interface at Hark | TechCrunch
archive.summary: Former Apple designer joins Hark, Brett Adcock's new AI startup developing custom hardware and interfaces for personal intelligence products. The company plans to design multimodal AI models, hardware, and user interfaces in tandem to create a "seamless end-to-end" experience that anticipates user needs.

archive.title: Inside OpenAI's talent pipeline: See who's feeding and hiring away workers at Sam Altman's AI giant
archive.summary: Analysis of OpenAI's hiring patterns reveals the company has aggressively recruited from major tech companies, particularly Google and Apple, as it builds its hardware and AI capabilities. Many former OpenAI employees subsequently moved to smaller AI startups, creating a talent pipeline that extends Sam Altman's influence across the industry.

archive.title: A $373 Clock With No Hands Sounds Wild Until You See It
archive.summary: Jony Ive's latest design—a $373 handless clock—exemplifies the former Apple design chief's continued pursuit of radical minimalism in consumer products. The timepiece removes traditional clock hands entirely, demonstrating the kind of confident design philosophy that defined Ive's tenure at Apple and now characterizes his independent work at LoveFrom.
